outgoing.explanation: The probate and parish-index negatives bear directly on the unresolved origin-and-parentage question: they searched for the emigrant, father Francis, and family without producing the record that would close the question.
The Norfolk parish and marriage negative bears directly on the first-wife question by finding no matching John Gurney and Mary marriage or household in the searched English collections.

The probate and parish negatives sharpen both sides of the Candidate B weighing: they do not supply the desired positive family record, while also documenting the record gap the current probability estimate must live with.

The completed probate and Norfolk-index negatives reduce the remaining value of further searching to the specific named levers rather than an open-ended expectation that ordinary indexed records will solve the case.

The broader probate, parish, and marriage negatives corroborate the no-family-signature finding while keeping it framed as an indexed/surviving-record gap rather than evidence the family was outside England.

statement: The English probate courts and Norfolk parish/marriage indexes, searched for any record naming the emigrant, his father Francis, or his family, return no positive match. No Francis Gurney G14 will survives in the Commissary, Archdeaconry, Prerogative, or Norwich courts; the two Rattlesden Rivett wills name no Margaret and no Gurney; and the Norfolk parish and same-name indexes yield no John-son-of-Francis baptism and no matching household for John or his wife Mary.
